title: Rookwood outbound play journal
content:
Topline: sketching an outbound + pilot play for Rookwood (mid-market retail chain, ~120 stores). Goal: pilot on checkout assistant + inventory Q&A with Dedicated or Hosted API depending on data sensitivity.

Quick account notes (raw):
- HQ in Denver, points of contact: Head of Product (Avery Cole), Director Ops (Jamal Park), CIO (Elena Martinez).
- Tech stack: AWS (VPC), backend: Node + Postgres, storefronts: React Native POS, ERP: BrightMerchant (custom integrations).
- Recent public: Series B (2024), raised for automation and store efficiencies — likely receptive to productivity pilots.
- Pain: long hold times for store managers, frequent manual inventory lookups, inconsistent upsell at POS.
- Compliance: handles PII (loyalty info), but subset exposure OK for hosted if scrubbed; otherwise Dedicated within their VPC.

Why Redwood fits (hypothesis):
- Need predictable latency at POS -> Redwood Dedicated can offer reserved capacity and latency SLOs.
- Mixed workload: short lookup queries (embeddings/rerank) + conversation flows (chat/generation). Redwood's mult-mode serving + caching helps keep token costs down.
- Want rollout controls and observability for business KPIs (conversion lift, handle time). Console + rollout features are relevant.

Pilot proposal (30–45 day):
1) Scope: Checkout assistant that: a) answers inventory/price queries, b) suggests 1–2 upsells, c) returns structured response for POS to render quick actions.
2) Data: static product metadata + anonymized sales logs sample. Option A: Hosted with data scrub + gateway. Option B: Dedicated in customer's account (preferred for security).
3) Metrics: average response latency (<150ms p95), accuracy on inventory queries (>92%), uplift in add-on conversion (+3–5%), reduced manager escalations (-20%).
4) Success criteria: pilot hits latency + accuracy targets and product team signs for 3-store rollout.
5) Timeline: week 1 data ingest & baseline; week 2 fine-tune prompts + model variant tests; week 3 soft roll in 1 store; weeks 4–6 metric monitoring & adjustments.

Outbound messaging (cold -> warm):
- Cold Subject options:
  - "Small pilot: speed up checkout + increase add-on conversion at Rookwood stores"
  - "Can we cut inventory lookup time at POS by 50%?"
- 1st line: "Hey <Name> — quick note: we helped a 90-store retailer reduce manager lookup time by 40% using a tiny LLM pilot that plugs into existing product metadata. Wondering if Rookwood would be open to a 4–6 week experiment?"
- Value bullets (for pitch):
  - deploy in 2–3 weeks with minimal engineering (webhook + product csv),
  - transparent perf and cost breakdowns (token-level),
  - failover to simpler APIs when latency spikes,
  - dedicated capacity option for committed performance.
- CTA: "15-min sync to walk through a test plan? I can bring an engineer."

Phone script (brief):
- Intro: "Hi <Name>, Maya from Redwood Inference — we've been doing short pilots that plug into POS to answer staff questions and push targeted add-ons. I wanted to ask two quick questions: 1) what takes your team the most time at checkout; 2) do you have internal guardrails for testing new inference tech?"
- If they say compliance concerns -> pivot to Dedicated or data-scrubbing + on-prem pitch.

Objection handling (notes):
- "We can't send data to 3rd party": offer Dedicated in VPC + explicit KMS/HSM options; propose data minimization (only product ids + inventory counts) and local caching.
- "LLMs hallucinate": emphasize reranking with deterministic SKU/price resolver + structured output schema that requires explicit match to catalog ids. Also show eval on held-out queries.
- "Cost concerns": show Redwood Optimize suggestions: batching, prefix caching for common queries, and quantized model variant with similar quality for much lower cost.
- "Integration effort": show lightweight webhook + adaptor pattern; sample repo: github.com/redwood-inference/integrations/pos-sample.

Technical execution notes for engineering handoff:
- Minimal API surface: POST /query -> {type: inventory|upsell, context: {store_id, last_6_sales}, query_text}
- Response schema: {verbatim: string, matches: [{sku, confidence}], suggested_actions: [{label, payload}]}
- Cache strategy: prefix cache keyed by (store_id, sku) for inventory lookups; use TTL 5–10s for high-turnover items.
- Model candidates: small chat-optimized base (quantized) for generation + an embeddings model for semantic SKU search. Evaluate both latency and token cost.

Risks / open questions:
- How often does their catalog change? (if daily, cache invalidation needs ops hooks)
- POS offline scenarios — need local fallback with last-known snapshot.
- Who owns the customer-facing success metric internally? (Ops vs Product)
- Any vendor restrictions in procurement (must be on AWS Marketplace)?

Experiment variants (A/B ideas):
- Variant A: Suggest one upsell with price anchor; Variant B: suggest two micro-adds with confidence threshold.
- Variant C: UI-first fallback — show suggestions as non-intrusive tips; Variant D: proactive push after slow checkout.

Data checklist (asks for initial call):
- sample product catalog (CSV) + SKU mapping,
- POS logs (anonymized last 30 days) with store_id, sku, timestamp, transaction_total,
- list of quick-answers staff frequently ask (from ops),
- preferred AWS region and networking constraints.

Next steps (action list):
- [ ] Draft 15-min intro email and put on Jamal Park's calendar (target: next Wed)
- [ ] Prep 1-pager pilot brief (ops + security elevator pitch) — Maya
- [ ] Engineering kickoff: pair with Ethan for sample adaptor + data ingestion script
- [ ] Send compliance checklist and Dedicated option cost outline if they push on security

Notes to self: keep outreach friendly but technical—Rookwood ops care about measurable store efficiency. Use concrete numbers from past pilots; attach short demo video (30–60s) in follow-ups. If they ask for procurement timeline, propose a short PO-friendly trial (30 days) to accelerate decisioning.

Scratch ideas / snippets to reuse:
- Email snippet for operations lead: "We prototype a single use case in less than a month — no model training, just prompt engineering + catalog alignment. If it drives store efficiency we scope a dedicated rollout."
- Objection short-circuits: "We can run the pilot in your VPC if preferred; you always own the keys."

End of journal entry.
